title: Plant metabolism in a dynamic temperature regime.
authors: Tung Lo, Wing; Bagshaw, Sophia Bianca; Brodsky, Vladimir; Suling, Bianca Emily; Nagele, Thomas
one_liner_zh: 综述植物代谢对温度变化的调控，涉及转录因子和机器学习，但未聚焦蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，仅间接相关。
abstract: Many plant species can efficiently adjust their metabolism to a changing temperature regime. As growth temperature significantly influences plant development, growth and distribution, it is of utmost importance to reveal how metabolism is linked to genetic regulation and phenotypic output. Key regulatory mechanisms include transcription factors which mediate responses to low and elevated temperatures, integrating signals related to carbon and nitrogen balance. Advances in high-throughput experimental techniques, mathematical modeling, and machine learning have deepened our understanding of gene regulatory networks, metabolic compartmentation, and the feedback loops between metabolism and gene expression. However, the complex, highly compartmentalized structure of plant cells poses challenges for interpreting metabolic regulation, particularly regarding subcellular allocation of sugars and energy signaling pathways. This review aims at identifying limitations of both experimental and computational analysis of plant metabolism which currently prevent the generation of predictive models of plant physiology in a changing temperature regime. Advances of machine learning and multi-omics integration are discussed in context of how genome sequence information can be linked to metabolic and phenotypic outcomes.
abstract_zh: 许多植物物种能够高效地调整其代谢以适应变化的温度环境。由于生长温度显著影响植物的发育、生长和分布，揭示代谢如何与遗传调控及表型输出相关联至关重要。关键调控机制包括介导对低温和高温响应的转录因子，这些因子整合了与碳氮平衡相关的信号。高通量实验技术、数学建模和机器学习的发展加深了我们对基因调控网络、代谢区室化以及代谢与基因表达之间反馈循环的理解。然而，植物细胞复杂且高度区室化的结构对解释代谢调控构成挑战，特别是在糖的亚细胞分配和能量信号通路方面。本综述旨在识别当前阻碍在变化温度环境下生成植物生理预测模型的实验和计算分析中的局限性。文中讨论了机器学习和多组学整合的进展，以及基因组序列信息如何与代谢和表型结果相关联。
